boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten named SUNY Oneonta destinations for studying, gathering, recreation, and campus programming, documented by current university sources.

cards.title: James M. Milne Library
cards.subtitle: Campus library and academic-support hub
cards.notes: Start on the floor that fits your task: use quiet areas for focused work, meeting rooms for collaboration, and the labs for technology needs.
cards.short_summary: A five-floor library with quiet study, group rooms, technology labs, and academic-support services.
cards.evidence_claim: SUNY Oneonta describes Milne Library as having quiet study areas, group meeting rooms, computer and technology labs, and the Student Learning Center.
cards.access_notes: Campus map lists Milne Library as Building 32. Check library hours before visiting.

cards.title: Milne Library Social Zone
cards.subtitle: First floor of Milne Library
cards.notes: Bring a project partner for first-floor group work, then move to one of the library’s quieter areas when you need to read or write solo.
cards.short_summary: A colorful, comfortable first-floor area intended for group work.
cards.evidence_claim: SUNY Oneonta identifies the Social Zone on Milne Library’s first floor as a colorful, comfortable space for group work.
cards.access_notes: Located inside Milne Library; follow current library access rules and hours.

cards.title: Milne Library Reading Room
cards.subtitle: First floor, across from Dragon Tea
cards.notes: Use the comfortable seating to browse current print newspapers and periodicals, or take a short reading break between research tasks.
cards.short_summary: A first-floor reading room with seating and current print periodicals and newspapers.
cards.evidence_claim: SUNY Oneonta says the Milne Library Reading Room is on the first floor across from Dragon Tea and provides seating plus current print periodicals and newspapers.
cards.access_notes: Located inside Milne Library; follow current library access rules and hours.

cards.title: Hunt Union
cards.subtitle: Student-activities and events hub
cards.notes: Use the information desk as a practical first stop, then check the Union’s lounges, movie theater, game room, and scheduled events.
cards.short_summary: A central campus building with student amenities, event facilities, lounges, and services.
cards.evidence_claim: SUNY Oneonta calls Hunt Union the hub of student activities and events and lists amenities including a theater, game room, lounges, ballroom, computers, and printers.
cards.source_title: Faculty Student Development Guide | SUNY Oneonta
cards.access_notes: Campus map lists Hunt Union as Building 24. Event and amenity availability can vary.

cards.title: Dragon's Lair
cards.subtitle: Game room in Hunt Union
cards.notes: Meet up for the game room, then use the rest of Hunt Union’s lounges or event spaces if you want to keep the visit going.
cards.short_summary: The named game-room amenity within Hunt Union.
cards.evidence_claim: SUNY Oneonta lists Dragon's Lair as the game room among Hunt Union’s amenities.
cards.source_title: Faculty Student Development Guide | SUNY Oneonta
cards.access_notes: Located in Hunt Union; confirm current game-room availability with Union Services.

cards.title: Hunt Union Living Room
cards.subtitle: Hunt Union sitting area with pond views
cards.notes: Settle into the sitting area for a break between classes, and use its view of Hunt Union Pond as a low-key change of scenery.
cards.short_summary: A Hunt Union sitting area with a fireplace, TV, and views of the pond.
cards.evidence_claim: SUNY Oneonta identifies the Hunt Union Living Room as a place to view Hunt Union Pond and lists it as a sitting area with a fireplace and TV.
cards.access_notes: Located in Hunt Union; seating and event use may affect availability.

cards.title: Hunt Union International Lounge
cards.subtitle: Indoor Hunt Union space overlooking the pond
cards.notes: Choose this indoor lounge when you want a shared seating area with a view of Hunt Union Pond without needing to leave campus.
cards.short_summary: A named Hunt Union lounge with views toward Hunt Union Pond.
cards.evidence_claim: SUNY Oneonta names the International Lounge as one of the places where students can take in views of Hunt Union Pond.
cards.access_notes: Located in Hunt Union; follow posted building access guidance.

cards.title: Hunt Union Pond Dock
cards.subtitle: Outdoor seating by Hunt Union Pond
cards.notes: Take a short outdoor pause by the pond, keeping to the designated dock and following any posted conditions or campus safety guidance.
cards.short_summary: A designated dock beside Hunt Union Pond for taking in the campus view.
cards.evidence_claim: SUNY Oneonta specifically identifies the dock as a place to take in views of Hunt Union Pond.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor conditions and posted campus guidance determine access.

cards.title: Campus Meditation Room
cards.subtitle: Campus wellness space
cards.notes: Use this room for a quiet reset between classes; plan around its current access arrangements and keep the space calm for other users.
cards.short_summary: A campus meditation space mentioned among SUNY Oneonta’s common gathering and wellness areas.
cards.evidence_claim: SUNY Oneonta identifies the Campus Meditation Room as a place students can use when away from residence halls and classes.
cards.access_notes: Confirm current location and availability with Student Affairs before visiting.

cards.title: College Camp
cards.subtitle: 119 Hoffman Road, SUNY Oneonta
cards.notes: Plan a daytime hike, picnic, or snowshoe outing on the camp property, and follow the site’s rules, gate schedule, and activity requirements.
cards.short_summary: A 276-acre university recreational and educational property with outdoor activities and trails.
cards.evidence_claim: SUNY Oneonta describes College Camp as a 276-acre former farm and woodland property for educational, recreational, and social opportunities; its activities page lists hiking, snowshoeing, and more.
cards.access_notes: Open daily 8 a.m.–8 p.m.; the main gate locks at 8 p.m. SUNY Oneonta faculty, staff, students, and alumni are authorized users.
